partners.diseaseBName: metabolic myopathy due to lactate transporter defect
partners.mechanism_chain: ITGA3 (HGNC:6204) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin cell surface interactions (GO:0007101); Integrin cell surface interactions (GO:0007101) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cellular proliferation (HP:0002104); SLC16A1 (HGNC:11040) —DISRUPTS→ Lactate transport (GO:0015279); Lactate transport (GO:0015279) —DECREASES→ Lactate (CHEBI:15361); Lactate (CHEBI:15361) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Loss-of-function mutations in ITGA3 disrupt integrin-mediated cell signaling pathways, potentially affecting cellular proliferation and contributing to disease phenotype A. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in SLC16A1 impair lactate transport, leading to lactate accumulation and cellular energy deficits, manifesting as metabolic myopathy (disease B). The convergence lies in the shared consequence of disrupted cellular homeostasis and energy metabolism, impacting cellular function and leading to distinct but related phenotypic outcomes.

partners.mechanism_chain: CAV1 (HGNC:13450) —DISRUPTS→ Caveolae formation and lipid transport regulation (GO:0031245); Caveolae formation and lipid transport regulation (GO:0031245) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital generalized lipodystrophy (HP:0000964); ITGA3 (HGNC:6074) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin signaling and cell adhesion (GO:0007160); Integrin signaling and cell adhesion (GO:0007160) —LEADS_TO→ Laminin gamma-2 deficient epidermolysis bullosa (HP:0030947). Haploinsufficiency of CAV1 disrupts caveolae formation and lipid transport regulation, leading to congenital generalized lipodystrophy. Separately, haploinsufficiency of ITGA3 disrupts integrin signaling and cell adhesion, leading to laminin gamma-2 deficient epidermolysis bullosa. The overlap is conceptual, in that both genes are critical regulators of cellular structure and function, impacting distinct but essential cellular pathways.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. epidermolysis bullosa, junctional 6, with pyloric atresia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.474)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-210991, Reactome:R-HSA-216083, Reactome:R-HSA-3000157)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITGA3 (HGNC:6086) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-3/alpha-6 mediated signaling (GO:0007252); ITGA6 (HGNC:6090) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin alpha-3/alpha-6 mediated signaling (GO:0007252); Integrin alpha-3/alpha-6 mediated signaling (GO:0007252) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin development (HP:0002211); Integrin alpha-3/alpha-6 mediated signaling (GO:0007252) —LEADS_TO→ Pyloric atresia (HP:0002086); Integrin alpha-3/alpha-6 mediated signaling (GO:0007252) —LEADS_TO→ Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (HP:0011211). Loss-of-function mutations in ITGA3 and ITGA6 disrupt the integrin alpha-3/alpha-6 mediated signaling pathway, leading to a spectrum of phenotypes including abnormal skin development, junctional epidermolysis bullosa, and pyloric atresia.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in ITGA3 and ITGA6 do not converge on a common downstream signaling pathway impacting skin and gastrointestinal development, or if distinct downstream effectors are identified for each gene leading to their respective phenotypes. _(variant: gnomad allele frequency > 0.01 for variants in coding regions of ITGA3 or ITGA6.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of integrin signaling in these distinct rare diseases could reveal common therapeutic targets for interventions aimed at improving skin barrier function and gastrointestinal development, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 2. hereditary spastic paraplegia 75  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.433)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-210991)

**Proposed mechanism:** MAG (HGNC:6864) —DISRUPTS→ Myelin maintenance (GO:0048787); Myelin maintenance (GO:0048787) —LEADS_TO→ Leukodystrophy (HP:0001289); Myelin maintenance (GO:0048787) —LEADS_TO→ Spastic paraplegia (HP:0002506). Loss-of-function mutations in MAG disrupt myelin maintenance pathways, leading to the shared phenotype of leukodystrophy and the specific phenotype of spastic paraplegia.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with MONDO:0013881 or MONDO:0014729 caused by variants in genes other than MAG, or variants in MAG that do not lead to loss-of-function. _(variant: Any pathogenic loss-of-function variant in MAG present at a frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MAG in myelin maintenance could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting common downstream pathways for both MONDO:0013881 and hereditary spastic paraplegia 75.

#### 3. metabolic myopathy due to lactate transporter defect  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.410)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-210991)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITGA3 (HGNC:6204) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin cell surface interactions (GO:0007101); Integrin cell surface interactions (GO:0007101) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cellular proliferation (HP:0002104); SLC16A1 (HGNC:11040) —DISRUPTS→ Lactate transport (GO:0015279); Lactate transport (GO:0015279) —DECREASES→ Lactate (CHEBI:15361); Lactate (CHEBI:15361) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Loss-of-function mutations in ITGA3 disrupt integrin-mediated cell signaling pathways, potentially affecting cellular proliferation and contributing to disease phenotype A. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in SLC16A1 impair lactate transport, leading to lactate accumulation and cellular energy deficits, manifesting as metabolic myopathy (disease B). The convergence lies in the shared consequence of disrupted cellular homeostasis and energy metabolism, impacting cellular function and leading to distinct but related phenotypic outcomes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in ITGA3 do not affect cellular energy metabolism or lactate transport, or that mutations in SLC16A1 do not impact cellular proliferation or other pathways related to ITGA3 function. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the overlap in cellular modules affected by these distinct genetic defects could reveal common therapeutic targets for improving cellular energy metabolism or mitigating downstream effects of disrupted cellular signaling in both conditions.

#### 4. cystinuria  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.408)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-210991)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITGA3 (HGNC:6055) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal kidney physiology (HP:0000083); SLC7A9 (HGNC:10701) —DISRUPTS→ Cystine transport (GO:0015917); SLC3A1 (HGNC:10698) —DISRUPTS→ Cystine transport (GO:0015917); Cystine transport (GO:0015917) —DECREASES→ Cystine (CHEBI:17665); Cystine (CHEBI:17665) —LEADS_TO→ Cystinuria (HP:0003476). Mutations in ITGA3 lead to abnormal kidney physiology (Disease A). Separately, mutations in SLC7A9 or SLC3A1 disrupt the cystine transport pathway, leading to reduced intracellular cystine and subsequent cystinuria (Disease B). The shared mechanism is the disruption of normal renal cystine handling, impacting cellular redox and leading to distinct but related renal phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in ITGA3 do not impact renal physiology, or that SLC7A9 and SLC3A1 are not involved in renal cystine transport. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.01) in HGNC:6055 (ITGA3) or HGNC:10701 (SLC7A9)/HGNC:10698 (SLC3A1) associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of cystine transport in renal health could lead to novel therapeutic targets for both ITGA3-related disorders and cystinuria, potentially involving modulating cystine levels or transport mechanisms.

#### 5. exercise-induced hyperinsulinism  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.389)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-210991)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITGA3 (HGNC:6144) —DISRUPTS→ Integrin cell surface interactions (R-HSA-6809020); Integrin cell surface interactions (R-HSA-6809020) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin morphology (HP:0000951); SLC16A1 (HGNC:11070) —DISRUPTS→ Monocarboxylate transport (R-HSA-1947634); Monocarboxylate transport (R-HSA-1947634) —LEADS_TO→ Lactate (CHEBI:15361); Lactate (CHEBI:15361) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperinsulinism (HP:0011853); Monocarboxylate transport (R-HSA-1947634) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperinsulinism (HP:0011853). Loss-of-function mutations in ITGA3 disrupt integrin cell surface interactions, leading to abnormal skin morphology in MONDO:0013881. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in SLC16A1 impair monocarboxylate transport, affecting lactate metabolism and resulting in hyperinsulinism in exercise-induced hyperinsulinism. The convergence occurs at the level of cellular metabolic processes influenced by solute transport, specifically monocarboxylate transport, which can indirectly impact cellular homeostasis and downstream signaling pathways relevant to both disease modules.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in SLC16A1 are found to be causative for MONDO:0013881, or if mutations in ITGA3 are found to be causative for exercise-induced hyperinsulinism, this hypothesis would be falsified. Furthermore, if genetic studies reveal no significant overlap in affected pathways or metabolites related to monocarboxylate transport between the two diseases, the hypothesis would be weakened. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in the gnomAD database within the SLC16A1 gene that are associated with normal monocarboxylate transporter function would challenge the proposed mechanism for exercise-induced hyperinsulinism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic underpinnings, even if indirect, could reveal novel therapeutic targets. For instance, interventions aimed at modulating monocarboxylate transport or its downstream metabolic consequences might offer benefits for both conditions, or at least provide insights into the broader role of these pathways in human disease.

Loss-of-function mutations in SLC16A1 disrupt monocarboxylate transport, leading to the accumulation of monocarboxylate species. This accumulation contributes to ketoacidosis and intellectual disability observed in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in SLC16A1 with a dominant-negative effect or variants in other genes that directly cause ketoacidosis and intellectual disability without impacting monocarboxylate transport would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a high allele frequency (>0.1%) of loss-of-function variants in SLC16A1 in the general population would also challenge the causality of this gene for rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SLC16A1 in both diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring monocarboxylate transport or mitigating the downstream metabolic consequences, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 7. congenital generalized lipodystrophy type 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.375)

Separately, haploinsufficiency of ITGA3 disrupts integrin signaling and cell adhesion, leading to laminin gamma-2 deficient epidermolysis bullosa. While the genes and primary pathways are distinct, both CAV1 and ITGA3 play roles in complex cellular processes that, when disrupted, manifest as distinct rare diseases. The overlap is conceptual, in that both genes are critical regulators of cellular structure and function, impacting distinct but essential cellular pathways.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in CAV1 associated with MONDO:0013881, or a pathogenic variant in ITGA3 associated with congenital generalized lipodystrophy type 3, would falsify the hypothesis of distinct causal genes for these diseases. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct roles of ITGA3 and CAV1 in cellular processes and disease pathogenesis provides a foundation for exploring potential therapeutic strategies. While direct overlap is limited, insights from one disease might inform research into the other, particularly concerning cellular integrity and metabolic regulation.
